cards.title: Dictionaries map keys to values
cards.body: A dictionary stores pairs in curly braces. Look a value up by its key with square brackets.

cards.title: Adding and replacing
cards.body: Assigning to a key adds it, or replaces the old value if the key is already there.

cards.title: Is the key there?
cards.body: `key in d` is True when the dictionary has that key. Looking up a missing key with `[]` is an error, so check first.

cards.title: Two values from one line
cards.body: `a, b = line.split()` splits a line and stores the two pieces in two variables at once.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print Ada's age, 36, but crashes with a `KeyError`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Keys must match exactly, capitals too. The key is `"ada"`, so use `ages["ada"]`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Assigning to an existing key replaces its value.

exercise.prompt: The first line is a count N; then N lines of `name number`. The last line is a name: print its number, or `unknown` if it is not in the book. Store the book in a dictionary; if a name appears twice, the later number wins.
exercise.starterCode:
n = int(input())
book = {}
